title: Year 12 Investigating Science Module 6 – Technologies
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Investigating Science Module 6, organised by its two Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How does technology enhance or limit investigations?

questions.prompt: What type of technology displays a continuously varying measurement, often with a pointer or scale?
What type of technology displays measurements as discrete numerical values?
What term describes how close a measured value is to the accepted value?
What error causes measurements to scatter unpredictably around a value?
What error shifts measurements consistently in the same direction?
What process checks and adjusts a measuring instrument against a known standard?
What document gives hazard, handling and safety information for a chemical?
questions.answer: A Safety Data Sheet. Accept: SDS.

questions.prompt: What Australian workplace framework guides safe use of equipment and procedures?
questions.answer: Work Health and Safety. Accept: WHS.

questions.prompt: What variable is deliberately changed in an investigation?
What variable is measured using the selected technology?
What limitation occurs when an instrument cannot detect changes smaller than its smallest scale division?
What term describes the smallest change that a measuring device can reliably distinguish?

categories.name: How do science & technology drive each other?

questions.prompt: What imaging technique was crucial in revealing the structure of DNA?
What particle accelerator helped provide evidence for the Higgs boson?
questions.answer: The Large Hadron Collider. Accept: LHC.

questions.prompt: What technology allows scientists to imitate complex systems such as Earth’s geological history?
Detection of what phenomenon helped advance atomic theory?
What optical instrument was advanced by scientific understanding of refraction and reflection to view tiny objects?
What optical instrument uses reflection or refraction to observe distant astronomical objects?
Understanding radioactive decay contributed to what cancer treatment using ionising radiation?
Discovery of DNA structure drove development of what broad field for modifying organisms?
Newton’s laws inform engineering designed to make buildings resist what natural hazard?
What term describes harvesting biological resources to develop useful products?
Whose traditional knowledge of medicinal plants is specifically recognised as valuable to ethical bioharvesting in Australia?
questions.answer: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

questions.prompt: What word best describes the relationship in which advances in science drive technology and advances in technology drive science?

finalRound.prompt: What term describes the two-way relationship in which scientific knowledge drives new technologies and new technologies enable further science?
